Posterior predictive check summaries

ppcSummary.Rd

Compares observed counts with posterior predictive count samples from a fitted magComp model. Replicates are obtained from

fitted(object, target = "observation", type = "count",
       summary = "samples")$count

These use the original exposures when magnitude is fitted. fitted() returns these simulated observations; ppcSummary() compares replicate count summaries with the observed counts. Each call generates fresh replicates; it does not reuse a previously created prediction object or refit the model.

Usage

ppcSummary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'magComp'
ppcSummary(object,
                             type = NULL,
                             group = NULL,
                             probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted magComp object.

type

Summary scale: total count by sampling unit, total count by category, sampling-unit/category cell count, total count by group, or group/category count. The default is NULL: use "unit_total" when magnitude is fitted. Composition alone uses "unit_category".

group

Grouping variable required for "group_total" or "group_category". This can be a column name in the unit-level data or a vector with one value per sampling unit.

probs

Posterior predictive quantile probabilities.

...

Must be empty. Unknown arguments are rejected.

Details

Choose one supported type. Full models support all five checks. Magnitude-only models support "unit_total" and "group_total", using negative-binomial replicate totals. Composition-only models support "unit_category", "category_total", and "group_category", using multinomial allocations conditional on observed totals. Checking those fixed totals would not assess fit, so total checks are rejected. The printed output states this conditioning. The count_conditioning attribute also records it. Both fixed-area stems and point-sampling basal-area models are supported. For point sampling, checks compare observed and replicated in-tree tallies using each point's BAF. Group summaries add the observed counts and replicate counts from units in each group. These remain tally-count checks, including when BAF varies between points; they are not expanded stand estimates.

For each check, \(T\) is the observed count or sum of counts selected by type; \(T^{rep}\) is its replicate counterpart. The reported p_lower and p_upper estimate $$ p_{lower} = \Pr(T^{rep} \le T \mid \mathrm{data}), \qquad p_{upper} = \Pr(T^{rep} \ge T \mid \mathrm{data}). $$ They are computed as fractions of replicates across all retained draws and chains. The p_value column is a two-sided posterior predictive p-value: $$p_{two} = \min\{1,\, 2\min(p_{lower}, p_{upper})\}.$$ Ties contribute to both tails, so their probabilities need not sum to one.

A small p_lower indicates an unusually low observed count relative to the replicates; a small p_upper indicates an unusually high count. For example, p_upper = 0.02 gives p_value = 0.04 when the upper tail is the smaller one. A p_value near one indicates a central observed count. A reported zero means no simulated replicates reached that tail; it is not evidence that its probability is exactly zero.

These are Bayesian posterior predictive checks, not probabilities that the model is correct or incorrect. The same data inform the fit and the check; posterior predictive p-values are not generally uniform under the fitted model (Gelman, 2013), and a threshold such as 0.05 does not have the usual hypothesis-test calibration. Use small values to flag discrepancies for inspection, including their size and direction. Large values do not establish overall model adequacy. These checks concern the fitting data, not cross-validation performance.

The requested quantiles describe replicate observations, including sampling variation. They are not credible intervals for expected counts. Separately summarizing draws returned by fitted() gives the same kinds of quantities, with Monte Carlo differences because separate calls simulate separate replicates.

Replicate simulation uses R's current random-number state. Use set.seed() externally for reproducibility.

Value

A data frame with identification columns type, group, unit, and category, plus:

observed

The observed count or sum of counts.

mean

The posterior predictive replicate mean.

q...

Requested replicate quantiles; defaults are q2_5, q50, and q97_5.

p_lower, p_upper

Fractions of replicates at or below, and at or above, the observed value.

p_value

Twice the smaller tail fraction, capped at one.

n_draws

The number of replicate draws pooled across chains.

References

Gelman, A. (2013). Two simple examples for understanding posterior p-values whose distributions are far from uniform. Electronic Journal of Statistics, 7, 2595–2602. doi:10.1214/13-EJS854 .
